newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas to build new corporate office.
newsitem.headline: Adidas to build new corporate office.

text.p: Adidas AG said on Tuesday it will stay in Germany and build a new headquarters on a former American military base close to the Bavarian town where Adi Dassler founded the sportswear group in 1920.
Adidas said its existing corporate headquarters, a rambling complex of buildings that includes a former villa of Dassler, was too small for its growing workforce.
The new headquarters will be built on a former base called "Herzo Base" that was left vacant when the United States reduced its forces in Europe after the end of the Cold War.

Adidas has often denied talk it would move its headquarters out of the south German village of Herzogenaurach, or even Germany, since the group is led by Frenchman Robert Louis-Dreyfus, who saved Adidas from near-death in the early 1990s.

Adidas, best known for its three-striped logo, said it was in talks with the town of Herzogenaurch and a local real estate company to acquire the land. The new office is expected to be completed for the year 2000.

In addition to the new corporate headquarters, Adidas said the office complex will include a customer service centre, product showrooms, a conference centre, a research centre, museum, sports facilities and training centre for athletes.
